title: Prospect Sales Kit: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This prospect sales kit consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance, customer case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospective customers evaluating Redwood Inference. Use this doc when preparing discovery calls, executive briefings, and commercial proposals. The kit is intended for AEs, solution engineers, and sales engineers.

Key takeaways (what to memorize)
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform focused on production economics: predictable latency, low unit cost, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Core product pillars: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), Redwood Console (observability), Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit).
- Differentiators: production-grade runtime, unified developer experience across environments, cost-aware controls (batching, cache, quantization), and robust fallback/reliability features.

Elevator pitches
- 30-second (technical buyer): "Redwood gives engineering teams a single runtime and control plane to serve LLMs with predictable latency and cost — whether you want hosted API simplicity, reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or a private deployment for sensitive data. We optimize batching, caching, and quantization so you pay less per token without sacrificing latency or quality."
- 30-second (economic buyer): "Redwood reduces inference costs and operational risk. Customers see lower per-token spend through intelligent caching and model routing while preserving SLAs and auditability for regulated data."

Core positioning and target use-cases
- Best for product teams that need production SLAs, predictable unit economics, and the ability to run inference across hosted, reserved, and private infrastructure.
- Primary use cases: chat and assistants, document understanding (extraction & classification), embeddings and semantic search, summarization pipelines, and real-time personalization.

Competitive brief (summary)
- Compared to managed cloud endpoints: Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics (batching+cache+quantization) and multi-mode deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) with consistent tooling.
- Compared to turnkey API-first LLM providers: Redwood emphasizes operational controls and observability (per-route cost/latency, rollout controls).
- Compared to self-hosted inference frameworks: Redwood removes the heavy operations burden by offering a managed control plane, curated performance profiles, and SLA options for Dedicated.

Competitive matrix (high level)
- Feature comparisons to call out on deals:
  - Deployment modes: Redwood: hosted/dedicated/private (unified); Competitor A: hosted only; Competitor B: self-hosted runtime only.
  - Observability & cost breakdown: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing; others often lack integrated cost analytics.
  - Quality/regression tooling: Redwood supports prompt/eval-driven regression alerts tied to rollouts.
  - SLA & enterprise support: Redwood Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime and latency targets plus premium support tiers.

Pitch deck guidance (slide-by-slide)
1) Title slide — Customer name, meeting purpose, Redwood contact(s).
2) Executive summary — 1 slide with the problem we solve, expected outcomes (latency, cost reduction, reliability), and low-friction next steps.
3) Why Redwood — concise differentiation bullets (production-first, unified runtime, cost-aware controls).
4) How it works (high level) — runtime + orchestration, smart routing, caching/batching, deployment abstraction; include simple diagram.
5) Product modes & recommended fit — Hosted API for evaluation/fast MVP; Dedicated for predictable throughput and SLA buyers; Private for regulated workloads.
6) Performance & economics — benchmarking highlights (example: 30-250% effective token-cost reduction with caching/quantization for chat pipelines, and p95 latency targets <150ms for typical short-chat configs). Cite internal benchmark page.
7) Observability & ops — screenshots or callouts: per-route dashboards, alerting, rollout controls.
8) Security & compliance — KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, tenancy/isolation options.
9) Pricing guidance — high-level tiers and negotiation levers (see section below).
10) Case studies — 1-2 relevant examples with metrics.
11) Implementation plan & timeline — discovery → pilot → production rollout (typically 4-12 weeks depending on scope).
12) Ask & next steps — pilot contract, technical kickoff, PoC success criteria.

Pricing guidance (playbook)
- Pricing levers to present: usage-based hosted pricing (per-token + embedding units), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits), Professional Services (integration/privileged features), and Private deployment licensing/support.
- Common packaging recommendations:
  - MVP / PoC: Hosted API with 3 months of usage credits and a scoped evaluation plan (sample prompts, SLO targets, KPIs).
  - Mid-scale: Dedicated small pool + burst capacity, 6-12 month commit with cost discount.
  - Enterprise / Regulated: Private deployment + support + audit logging; negotiate term licensing and on-prem packaging fees.
- Negotiation playbook:
  1) Anchor on outcomes: predictable latency and unit economics, not just per-token sticker price.
  2) Offer staged discounts tied to committed throughput or multi-quarter consumption.
  3) Use Professional Services as a value add for integration, custom model onboarding, or compliance packaging.

Example pricing table (talking points only)
- Hosted: Pay-per-use; typical mid-market deal: $0.XX-$0.YY per 1k tokens (varies by model).
- Dedicated: Base monthly reserved GPU pool + usage for burst; effective price ~30-250% lower than hosted at scale (depending on utilization).
- Private: One-time licensing + annual support; custom quotes based on deployment footprint and support SLAs.

Case studies (select examples for prospects)
- Fintech startup (customer anonymized): Reduced inference cost by 42% for conversational flows after adopting Redwood Optimize caching & batching; improved p95 latency from 350ms to 140ms by switching to an optimized model variant and batch policy.
- Enterprise support portal (SaaS company): Migrated from ad-hoc self-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated; achieved SLA-backed uptime, centralized audit logs for SOC2 requirements, and standardized rollout controls across 3 product teams.
- Marketplace personalization (e-commerce): End-to-end deployment in 8 weeks; embeddings-based search latency improved and overall infra cost decreased by 28% with recommended quantization + batching profile.

Security FAQ for prospects (top questions and short answers)
Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted mode?
A: Hosted API encrypts data in transit and at rest; we provide scoped retention policies and offer configuration options for minimum retention. For higher assurance, customers should consider Dedicated or Private deployments where network isolation and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are available.

Q: Can customers bring their own KMS keys?
A: Yes — both Private deployments and Dedicated enterprise offerings support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and key rotation policies.

Q: Do you support SOC2 / ISO / GDPR compliance evidence?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II controls and provide compliance evidence and contract addendums for GDPR data processing needs. For regulated workloads, Private deployments enable additional controls.

Q: How are models audited or validated for PII leakage?
A: We recommend a multi-pronged validation: model evals during onboarding, prompt hygiene guidance, and monitoring/eval hooks in Redwood Console to detect regressions tied to prompt sets. For sensitive domains, we recommend Private deployments and tighter inspection during model onboarding.

Q: What isolation options exist between customers?
A: Hosted customers are logically isolated. Dedicated provides tenant-specific resource pools with stronger isolation guarantees; Private deployments offer full network isolation in customer VPCs or on-prem.

Handling common prospect objections
- "We host our models in-house to save money": Acknowledge the cost benefits but emphasize Redwood’s managed control plane, optimized runtime, and reduced engineering overhead. Offer a pilot showing total cost of ownership comparison across 3 months.
- "We’re worried about vendor lock-in": Highlight deployment portability (same API across hosted/dedicated/private), exportable configs, and the ability to pin model versions.
- "We need compliance evidence": Provide the security FAQ plus references to compliance-evidence pages and recommended Private deployment checklist.

Implementation timeline (typical)
- Week 0: Discovery & success criteria (data access, traffic profile, KPIs).
- Weeks 1-2: Pilot setup — test account, sample prompts, telemetry hooks.
- Weeks 3-6: Configuration tuning (batching cache policies, model/quantization selection), integration.
- Weeks 6-12: Production rollout, SLO tuning, handoff to customer ops.

Usage notes
- Keep the pitch deck concise: no longer than 12 slides for initial executive meetings.
- Customize case studies and metrics to the prospect’s vertical and scale.
- In technical pre-sales, include a short benchmark focused on the prospect’s anticipated sequence lengths and concurrency profile.
